<!-- Source page: Nix -->

While not immediately apparent, the name Nix refers to a number of different tools and concepts:

- <a href="Nix_(package_manager)" class="wikilink" title="Nix (package manager)">Nix (package manager)</a>: tooling for managing packages and build processes using the Nix language;
- <a href="Nix_(language)" class="wikilink" title="Nix (language)">Nix (language)</a>: a declarative language used for defining expressions that are evaluated by the various Nix tools;
- <a href="Nix_(command)" class="wikilink" title="Nix (command)">Nix (command)</a>: the new experimental CLI interface that aims to unify the various Nix commands;
- <a href="Nix_(command_line_utilities)" class="wikilink" title="Nix (command line utilities)">Nix (command line utilities)</a>: a set of CLI tools that evaluate Nix expressions with the goal of producing various builds;
- <a href="Nix_store" class="wikilink" title="Nix store">Nix store</a>: a place that can store file system data (such as packages), in particular, the Nix store found at `/nix/store`;
- The <a href="Nix_ecosystem" class="wikilink" title="Nix ecosystem">Nix ecosystem</a>, a set of tools and programs built upon the Nix language.

There are other related concepts that might also be relevant:

- <a href="Nixpkgs" class="wikilink" title="Nixpkgs">Nixpkgs</a>: a repository of Nix packages;
- <a href="NixOS" class="wikilink" title="NixOS">NixOS</a>: the Linux distribution built on top of the Nix package manager and Nixpkgs repository;
- <a href="NixOS_(command_line_utilities)" class="wikilink" title="NixOS (command line utilities)">NixOS (command line utilities)</a>: a set of CLI tools used in managing a NixOS installation.
